mauborgne-1915-challenge.summary: The first 499 letters of Article 29 of the Regulations annexed to Hague Convention IV (1907) on who is a spy, in the spelling the cipher letters give, stopping mid-sentence at 'for' where the key text ends; the contents say nothing about Mauborgne's own business, the choice of a legal text and a field-manual key are the contributor's finding. Mauborgne meant sealed envelopes with the plaintext and the method to be opened after three months; they are lost.

system: Running key with a rule of odd shifts: each plaintext letter is moved back by an odd number of places set by the key letter (c = p - (2*(k mod 13) + 1) mod 26, A=0; key letters A/N give 1, B/O give 3 ... M/Z give 25), so each cipher letter has the opposite…
